related_questions.question: How is child support determined in Virginia?

text_blocks.snippet: In Virginia, child support is primarily calculated using the "income shares model". This model considers the combined gross income of both parents and divides the support obligation proportionally based on each parent's income and the number of children. The court also takes into account other factors such as health insurance costs, work-related childcare expenses, and other necessary and reasonable expenses for the child.
snippet_highlighted_words: primarily calculated using the "income shares model"

list.snippet: The court will examine all sources of income for both parents to determine their gross monthly income.
This includes, but is not limited to, salaries, wages, commissions, and self-employment income.
The court may also impute income to a parent who is voluntarily unemployed or underemployed, meaning they could be earning more based on their potential earning capacity.
The court adds both parents' gross monthly incomes to arrive at a combined total.
The court uses Virginia's schedule of basic child support obligations to determine the total amount of support based on the combined income and number of children.
This schedule outlines the presumptive amount of child support, but the court may deviate from it under certain circumstances.
The total child support obligation is then divided between the parents based on their respective shares of the combined gross income.
For example, if one parent earns 60% of the combined income, they will be responsible for 60% of the child support obligation.
The court will also consider and allocate responsibility for expenses such as health insurance premiums, work-related childcare costs, and other necessary and reasonable expenses for the child.
In Virginia, there is a presumption that the parties will divide reasonable and necessary unreimbursed expenses proportionately, unless there's good cause or an agreement to the contrary.

While the income shares model is the standard, the court can deviate from the guidelines in certain situations, such as when one parent has significantly more or less time with the child than the other, or when there are other factors that make the guidelines unfair, according to the Surovell Isaacs & Levy, PLC.
A common reason for deviation is when one parent has a much higher or lower income than the other, even after the income shares model is applied.
Child support orders can be modified if there is a material change in circumstances, such as a change in income or custody arrangements.
If either parent's income changes, the child support order can be adjusted to reflect the new income levels, says James E. Short, Plc.

text_blocks.snippet: In Virginia, child support is determined using a mathematical formula outlined in the state's Child Support Guidelines, which are based on the income shares model. This model aims to ensure children receive the same financial support they would have if their parents lived together. Both parents are responsible for financially supporting their children, and the amount of support is typically determined by the court based on factors like combined gross income, the number of children, and the amount of time each parent spends with the child.
snippet_highlighted_words: child support is determined using a mathematical formula outlined in the state's Child Support Guidelines, which are based on the income shares model

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of Virginia child support laws:

list.title: Income Shares Model:
list.snippet: The core of Virginia's child support calculations is the income shares model. This model considers the combined gross income of both parents to determine the total support obligation.

list.title: Guidelines:
list.snippet: Virginia has established child support guidelines, which are a set of rules and formulas used to determine the appropriate amount of support. These guidelines create a rebuttable presumption that the calculated amount is the correct amount, but the court can deviate in special circumstances.

list.title: Factors Considered:
list.snippet: The guidelines consider various factors, including:
Parental Income: The combined gross income of both parents is a primary factor.
Number of Children: The number of children needing support is also considered.
Time with Each Parent: The amount of time each parent spends with the child can influence the support calculation.
Health Insurance: The cost of health insurance for the child is factored in.
Childcare Costs: Work-related childcare expenses are also considered.
Extraordinary Medical Expenses: Any extraordinary medical costs for the child may be factored in.

list.title: Duration of Support:
list.snippet: Generally, child support obligations continue until the child reaches 18 years of age. However, support may continue longer if the child is still in high school, is not self-supporting, and lives with the parent seeking support. Support can also extend beyond 18 for a child with a severe and permanent mental or physical disability.

list.title: Modifications:
list.snippet: Child support orders can be modified if there has been a substantial and unanticipated change in circumstances.

list.title: Minimum Support:
list.snippet: Virginia has a minimum child support obligation of $68 per month, even if a parent has limited or no income, unless there's a specific reason like SSI disability.

list.title: Enforcement:
list.snippet: The Virginia Division of Child Support Enforcement (DCSE) can assist with establishing, modifying, and enforcing child support orders.

list.title: Garnishment:
list.snippet: Unpaid child support can be collected through wage garnishment, with limits on the amount of disposable earnings that can be garnished.
